proposed_facts.reason: Canonical enumeration, initialization and operational guards compare exactly with -1, not every negative value. Accepted as explicitly source-level behavior, not proof of compiled .sdata identity.
DI rejection precedes the initialized-state test; initialization failure and external removal reset selection, whereas operational rejection does not. Compiled section mapping remains deferred.
The probe loop waits only on zero; ID retrieval and the matching-ID callback are separate conditions. The admitted scan returns true regardless of discovery.
Canonical branches confirm entry rejection, ordered scanning, no local timeout, channel-2 probe bypass and callback-controlled early success.
Five operations contribute to err through separate |= statements; EXIUnlock is called without incorporating its result.

RxCallback is assigned before locking; selected-path command, synchronization and DMA are all attempted, with no inline teardown. RxHandler uses current global state. Lower-level completion guarantees are appropriately deferred.
Write-side launch and TxHandler independently confirm the same exceptional ownership and mutable callback behavior, without establishing lower-level cancellation guarantees.

Initialization installs callback state before setup failures; rollback resets Chan and Dev only. ExtHandler leaves all three local callback slots intact while conditionally clearing EXI notification registration.

contradictions.reason: Accept the four unresolved section identity/type dispositions: declarations establish source types and initialization, and the header establishes callback signatures, but neither establishes compiled section membership, exact size or ordering. Existing supported source knowledge and names are retained without promoting those layout claims.
Accept both sentinel-related supersessions: generic negative/nonnegative descriptions are inaccurate, and DI rejection has precedence over the initialized-state shortcut.

Accept both enumeration supersessions: nonzero probe termination is not itself proof of readiness or discovery. Deferring broader EXIProbeEx return-value meanings preserves the exact owned-source behavior.
Accept the synchronous-read supersession: success does not include every cleanup result because unlock is excluded from the accumulator.

Accept both asynchronous supersessions: false does not establish absent DMA or released ownership. Callback assignments survive lock rejection, selected-path errors do not short-circuit DMA attempts, and handlers consult mutable global state. Completion/cancellation guarantees remain explicitly deferred to lower-level EXI review.

Accept the module-state supersession: initialization rollback and external removal reset selection without undoing local callback assignments. The document preserves this distinction and the exceptional cleanup branches.

unresolved: Compiled mappings of Chan to .sdata and Dev plus the callback slots to .sbss, including exact section size and ordering, remain unverified; source declarations are insufficient.
EXIProbeEx is described by its literal zero/nonzero handling without assigning readiness meanings to all return values.
Lower-level EXI DMA failure, completion and cancellation guarantees remain outside this acceptance, particularly across external removal or subsequent callback-slot overwrites.
